Subject: Dedicated reservation proposal: dynamic fleet commitment and warm-start schedule — HelixX

Alex / Priyanka,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a concise reservation proposal that aligns to the usage profile you shared (spiky inference for batch jobs + steady low-latency traffic for the web app). High-level options are below; full rationale and the capacity model are in the attached spreadsheet.

Key options we recommend you consider:
- Soft-floor baseline: 48 GPUs reserved (keeps persistent latency SLOs for web tier during business hours).
- Elastic burst pool: additional 32 GPUs available as burst capacity with a warm-start policy (30–60 minute pre-warm windows before anticipated nightly batches).
- Phased ramp: 48 -> 80 GPUs over 12 weeks; checkpoints at weeks 2, 6, and 12 to move to next tranche.
- Warm-start credits: 200 pre-warm GPU-hours included in the first 30 days to reduce cold-start latency for batch windows.

Ask: please confirm which option (A: conservative 48 baseline + 32 burst; B: aggressive 80 baseline) you prefer so we can lock pricing and build the final contract language.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-helixx-v1.pdf (proposal summary), helixx-capacity-model.xlsx (workload-based sizing).

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Soojin,

Appreciate the clear options. A couple quick clarifying questions before we loop procurement:
1) For the burst pool (32 GPUs) — what is the typical cold-start penalty if we exceed the warm-start window? Do you expect 30–60 minutes to be enough for our nightly 2AM job?
2) If we take option A, can we scale burst capacity by an additional 16 GPUs on a monthly cadence without a contract amendment?
3) Pricing: is the warm-start credit consumed only when we trigger pre-warm, or also when autoscaling automatically reclaims burst GPUs?

Also tagging procurement for contract cadence — we aim to get legal review by Jan 6.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform — HelixX
alex.zhao@helixx.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhao <alex.zhao@helixx.ai>, HelixX Procurement <procurement@helixx.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation proposal: dynamic fleet commitment and warm-start schedule — HelixX

Alex — short answers inline, then a suggested amendment to the proposal language to make these behaviors explicit.

1) Cold-start penalty: if a GPU needs to be provisioned cold (no pre-warm), typical additional latency for first few minutes of the batch window is ~30–90s per request depending on model size and KV cache warmup. For your nightly 2AM job, the recommended 60-minute pre-warm gives >95% warm cache coverage based on the usage traces you shared.

2) Burst scaling: yes — Option A includes a self-service burst-scaling knob up to +16 GPUs monthly without contract amendment; anything beyond that requires a 30-day notice and adjustment to the reserved baseline. We'll mark that in the contract as "monthly burst expansion up to 16 GPUs".

3) Warm-start credits: consumed only when you explicitly schedule a pre-warm window or when the system triggers a policy-driven warm-up tied to a scheduled batch (not on ephemeral autoscale reclaim). Autoscales that do not use pre-warm time are billed at burst-hour rates; pre-warm credits reduce the initial cost and accelerate readiness.

Suggested proposal amendment (for the price sheet): add a line — "Warm-start credits apply to scheduled pre-warm windows and system-initiated scheduled batch warm-ups; they do not apply to opportunistic autoscale events."

I'll update the attached proposal and capacity model with those clarifications and send an editable copy.

Cheers,
Soojin
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Alex Zhao <alex.zhao@helixx.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation proposal: dynamic fleet commitment and warm-start schedule — HelixX

Alex / Priya — adding a quick technical note from the runtime/ops side to set expectations for warm-start behavior and minimum viable baseline.

- Baseline sizing: the 48-GPU soft-floor corresponds to 12 concurrent web inference lanes + a modest KV cache headroom for spike absorption (based on median sequence length 512 and 20 TPS burst). This baseline preserves <120ms P95 under typical traffic.
- Warm-start mechanics: pre-warm spins up the serving runtime, populates KV caches with checkpointed prefixes, and pins appropriate CUDA kernels ahead of the job. It takes approx 25–40 minutes to reach stable token-throughput for the largest model we discussed (30B variant).
- Staged ramp considerations: we recommend the 12-week tranche cadence be governed by production telemetry checkpoints (latency, sustained throughput, and token burn). If HelixX observes sustained 15% QoQ growth in token consumption across the web tier, we auto-trigger the next tranche.

Operational asks for HelixX team before go-live:
1) Provide two representative nightly job windows for the first 8 weeks so we can refine pre-warm scheduling policies.
2) Share retention requirements for KV cache snapshots (if you need longer retention we will size additional storage/memory).

Happy to run a short runbook review with your SREs next week.

—Karthik
Director, Runtime Ops — Redwood Inference
From: HelixX Procurement <procurement@helixx.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation proposal: dynamic fleet commitment and warm-start schedule — HelixX

Soojin / Redwood team,

Thanks for the clear proposal and the clarifications. Procurement reviewed the pricing sheet and the burst-scaling language; we can provisionally accept Option A (48 GPU baseline + 32 GPU burst pool) subject to the following items to be included in the SOW and MSA:

- Add the warm-start credit definition exactly as proposed by Redwood.
- Monthly burst expansion: +16 GPUs self-service; beyond that requires 30-day notice and mutual agreement.
- SLA: P95 latency target for web tier to be 150ms; credits for breach to be defined in the SLA schedule.
- Onboarding: a 6-week onboarding window with two runbook sessions; Redwood to provide a pre-warm scheduling pattern by week 1.
- Pricing redline: please add a line-item for pre-warm credit overages (priced per GPU-hour at burst rate).

Once Redwood incorporates those clauses into the contract draft, we will issue a PO. We aim to complete legal review by Jan 6 and have a Jan 15 go-live for the onboarding work.

Regards,
HelixX Procurement
procurement@helixx.ai
